events.title: Romulus Augustulus is proclaimed western Roman emperor
events.description: The general Orestes installed his young son Romulus as emperor in the West. Less than a year later Odoacer deposed him, an event conventionally taken as the end of the Western Roman Empire.
events.html: The general Orestes installed his young son Romulus as emperor in the West. Less than a year later Odoacer deposed him, an event conventionally taken as the end of the Western Roman Empire.

events.title: Martin Luther issues his Ninety-five Theses
events.description: Martin Luther sent his Ninety-five Theses against the sale of indulgences to the Archbishop of Mainz and, by tradition, posted them on the church door at Wittenberg. The debate they sparked became the Reformation.
events.html: Martin Luther sent his Ninety-five Theses against the sale of indulgences to the Archbishop of Mainz and, by tradition, posted them on the church door at Wittenberg. The debate they sparked became the Reformation.

events.title: Nevada becomes the 36th US state
events.description: Nevada was admitted to the Union during the Civil War, with Republicans keen on its votes for Lincoln's re-election and support for the 13th Amendment. It is still called the 'Battle Born State'.
events.html: Nevada was admitted to the Union during the Civil War, with Republicans keen on its votes for Lincoln's re-election and support for the 13th Amendment. It is still called the 'Battle Born State'.

events.title: Britain and France begin bombing Egypt over Suez
events.description: British and French aircraft attacked Egyptian airfields after Egypt rejected their ultimatum to withdraw from the Suez Canal zone. US and Soviet pressure forced a humiliating withdrawal.
events.html: British and French aircraft attacked Egyptian airfields after Egypt rejected their ultimatum to withdraw from the Suez Canal zone. US and Soviet pressure forced a humiliating withdrawal.

events.title: Indira Gandhi is assassinated by her bodyguards
events.description: Two Sikh bodyguards shot Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in her Delhi garden, months after she ordered the army into the Golden Temple at Amritsar. Anti-Sikh violence that followed killed about 3,000 people.
events.html: Two Sikh bodyguards shot Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in her Delhi garden, months after she ordered the army into the Golden Temple at Amritsar. Anti-Sikh violence that followed killed about 3,000 people.

events.title: World population reaches seven billion, UN estimates
events.description: The United Nations designated 31 October 2011 as the symbolic day the world's population reached seven billion. The total had doubled since the late 1960s.
